ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, and $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$. If $\angle AOE=160^\circ$ and $\angle COD=25^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle AOB$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$,\\
it follows that $\angle COE=2\angle COD=2\times 25^\circ=50^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle AOC=\angle AOE-\angle COE=160^\circ-50^\circ=110^\circ$,\\
also, since $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=\frac{1}{2}\times 110^\circ=\boxed{55^\circ}$.
